note: Fails four of five. He is a salaried IT technician, not a business owner or physician — and the business he did own, a photography practice, he closed in early 2026 precisely because it could not support his family: 'I don't have enough income to afford the baby, so I have to find a job.' Income fails decisively: he can reach roughly 100 to 200 euros a month, has just paid for a wedding and honeymoon, has a four-month-old, and his savings are earmarked for a house deposit. On starting point he is rescue rather than good-to-great — 90 kg targeting 75 kg after a full year of no training at all — and at 1.70 m and 90 kg he is close enough to the stated exclusion that it should be counted against him, even though he is not gym-averse and trained willingly before. The only clean match is neglected health, and he articulated it well: 'the body part is a huge part because it's deeply linked with mind and health.' The operational point is more useful than the classification: he was a cold Instagram lead who booked himself with no setter and no financial qualification, and consumed roughly two hours of closer time across two calls before anyone asked what he could pay. Whatever the ICP says on paper, the intake path is not applying it.
